items.title: Media adapters load in kohya, PEFT and full-difference formats and apply unmerged at run time, with a strength per request

steps.title: Adapters run unmerged, y = xW + s(xA)B with the low-rank branch at the adapter's precision, so strength changes per request without rewriting weights
steps.rationale:
overgo serves image adapters merged (docs/MOSS_IMAGE.md). The DMD LoRAs warn that merging into BF16 discards most of the distillation, because the delta is near BF16's rounding step, so the eight-step adapters need an unmerged path kept at their own precision. ComfyUI's ModelPatcher records patches per key with a backup and shares one module between clones; the shape is taken from that description, not its code.

Note: Absorbs media-lora/formats (retired 2026-11-11): reading each format's patch has no production caller until an adapter is applied while serving, which this step does, so the two land together, split by their first consumer. Read on 2026-11-11 from the imported files and the ComfyUI install's code:
- The three formats: 8-steps-dmd2-lora is kohya, lora_up [out, 128] and lora_down [128, in] in F32 with an alpha tensor (128, its metadata saying rank 128), on layers.N.proj.q, k, v and o, each its own; moss_image_sft is kohya in F16 on the fused layers.N.proj.qkv, o, ffn_up_gate and ffn_down and on final_linear_video, shared_block_modulation and text_embedder.proj, with full deltas .diff for the norms (norm1, norm2, q_norm, k_norm, final_norm_video, the text embedder's) and .diff_b for biases, its metadata naming it inverted from moss_image_sft.safetensors; moss-control is PEFT, lora_A [64, in] and lora_B [out, 64] in BF16, alpha 64 in its metadata, on q, k, v, o and the FFNs and on the text embedder's blocks, and carries a full video_embedder.weight [3072, 384] and bias that replace the input layer's [3072, 128]. Names may carry a diffusion_model. prefix, which a graph's names do not.
- Fused slices run both ways: overgo's graph reads q, k and v apart (as MOSS-Image SFT names them, and as moss-ultra-import/convrot splits the fused qkv), so a q adapter applies to q directly, and the SFT adapter's qkv delta, [9216, 3072], splits into thirds; in ComfyUI the q, k and v adapters land on slices of the fused weight.
- ComfyUI's patched weight (comfy/model_patcher.py patch_weight_to_device): the weight is dequantized in the LoRA compute dtype, comfy.lora.calculate_weight adds strength * alpha / rank * (up @ down), or the diff, then a quantized layer's set_weight re-encodes it with a recalculated scale and stochastic rounding seeded by the weight's name (comfy/ops.py, requantize_from_float). That seeded rounding is torch's generator, which no Go code reproduces, and it is what serving unmerged avoids; the golden is calculate_weight's float result before re-encoding, its float32 sums held as moss-ultra-import/convrot holds comfy_kitchen's: overgo computes the exact value, and the golden records how far ComfyUI's lies from it.

Serves: setup-steps; media-lora/moss-eight-step, krea-loras, sensenova-fast and moss-ultra-sections/depth-control apply adapters through it.
Disappears: merging as the only way to serve an adapter.
Evidence: at strength 1 an unmerged adapter's output matches the same adapter merged at F32 within a declared tolerance, and a second strength needs no reload.
Batch: device lane.

items.title: A ComfyUI recorder runs a saved workflow in ComfyUI's own process and records each section's settings, sigmas, latents and images as goldens, first the MOSS Ultra workflow

steps.title: Each recording holds its samplers' sigmas, the time of each step, the model files' hashes, and the workflow's prompt modes 2 and 3
steps.rationale:
Serves: setup-steps; the rest of what comfy-recorder/record's rationale names, which the 2026-11-11 recordings do not hold.

The recordings of 2026-11-11 keep each section's request hash, the inputs set over it, ComfyUI's version and the commits of it and each node pack, the final prompts (each PreviewAny node's text), the final latent (a SaveLatent after the section's KSampler), every picture by its SHA-256, the run's whole time, the card's most memory in use and the nodes answered from ComfyUI's cache. They do not hold: the sigmas each sampler ran, the time each step took, each model file's SHA-256 as ComfyUI loaded it, and the workflow's prompt modes 2 and 3, which the sections were recorded in mode 1 alone.

The change: the recorder reads ComfyUI's progress events over its websocket for the time each step took; each sampler's sigmas are recorded by a node of ComfyUI's own that outputs them (BasicScheduler, or KSampler's scheduler and steps read through ComfyUI's /object_info and the sigmas computed by a node added beside it, whichever ComfyUI's install holds), saved as a file; the model files' hashes are those moss_ultra_import.json pins, named by the recording with the install's paths read through ComfyUI's /models; and each prompt mode is recorded by the input that selects it, set over the section's own.

Check: TestTheUltraRecordingsAgreeAndParseStrictly, widened to hold each recording to its sigmas, its step times, its model hashes and the three prompt modes.

Batch: device lane; a recording runs only while no reading holds the card.

Note: 2026-11-13, findings this step carries (the lead's answer): SQA-345 (P2), the recorder reads the request ComfyUI itself exports for a workflow, under the section and source owner, and the separate UI compiler (flatten.go, widgets.go, workflow.go) goes, a malformed or missing request refused before the reference runs; SQA-388 (P2), the recorder admits its destination before it posts, records the accepted prompt's id with its request at once, and resumes that id through history after an interruption, never posting an unchanged accepted request again.

steps.title: Depth Anything V2 Small runs on internal/vitencoder with a DPT head, its depth map within one 8-bit level of the recorded one
steps.rationale:
The owner decided on 2026-11-05 that the workflow's depth estimator is built in overgo. depth_anything_v2_vits.pth is read with internal/pytorchzip. Its encoder is DINOv2 ViT-S/14 without registers, so its options are added to internal/vitencoder and no second ViT is written; the DPT head is written from the Depth Anything V2 paper and its Apache-2.0 code. Pre- and post-processing follow the workflow's DepthAnythingV2Preprocessor from comfyui_controlnet_aux (Apache-2.0): resolution 512, a size that is a multiple of 14, scaling to 8 bits, white for near.

Serves: a capability of its own, depth from any image, which vace-control's depth mode reuses.

steps.title: Depth control concatenates the VAE-encoded, normalised map times strength to the noise channels for the first half of sigma, through the control adapter's widened input layer

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
